questions.solution:
Higher the lattice energy lower the solubility. Out of the four combinations possible, the lattice energy of MgS (bi-bivalent ionic solid) is higher than those of Na2S, MgCl2 (uni-bivalent or biuni-valent ionic solids ) and NaCl (univalent ionic solids) and hence, MgS is the least soluble. Thus, due to higher charge/ion, the lattice formed between Mg2+ and S2- is very strong.
As lattice energy overweighs the hydration energy here, the salt is least soluble.

questions.q: Which of the following does not apply to bonding in metals ?
questions.solution:
Metallic bonding is not directional like covalent bonding, it is like ionic bonding in the sense that the force of attraction between the positive metal ions and the mobile electrons acts in every direction about the fixed (immobile) metal ions of the metal crystal lattice, but in ionic lattices none of the ions is mobile - a big difference between a metal bond and an ionic bond.

The outer electrons (–) from the original metal atoms are free to move around between the positive metal ions formed (+).
These 'free' or 'delocalised' electrons from the outer shell of the metal atoms are the 'electronic glue' holding the particles together.There is a strong electrical force of attraction between these free electrons (mobile electrons or 'sea' of delocalised electrons) (–) and the 'immobile' positive metal ions (+) that form the giant lattice and this is the metallic bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is false about covalent bonds?
options: The electrons are shared between atoms to get stable electronic arrangement.
The strength of the bond depends upon the extent of overlapping.
The bond may or may not be polar.
questions.solution:
Covalent bond is formed by the sharing of electrons or combining the atomic orbitals to form the hybrid orbitals. Hybrid orbitals have the more probability of electron density at one end of the orbital while others end the probability of finding the electron is negligible. Due to this, all covalent bonds are directional in nature.

The strength of the bond depends on the extent of overlapping. More overlapping then stronger will be the bond. 

If the electrons are sharing between the two same kinds of atoms then it will form a non-polar molecule. Eg:- H2, N2, and F2 etc.

If the sharing of electrons between the two different kinds of elements then the more electronegative element attracts shared pair of electrons towards itself and gets the partial negative charge corresponding the less electronegative atom carries the partial positive charge. Due to this, there is one dipole generated and these molecules known as polar molecules by consisting polar covalent bonds. Eg:- HCl

questions.solution:
If the given molecule/atom/ion has all paired electrons in its orbitals, then it is said to be diamagnetic and if atleast one of the orbital has unpaired electron, then it is said to be paramagnetic.

Writing the molecular orbital configuration of the given molecules assuming that no 2s-2p mixing takes place-

(i) Be2→σ1s2, σ*1s2, σ2s2, σ*2s2 (diamagnetic)

(ii) B2→σ1s2, σ*1s2, σ2s2, σ*2s2,σ2pz2 (diamagnetic)

(iii) C2→σ1s2, σ*1s2, σ2s2, σ*2s2, σ2pz2,π2px1π2py1 (paramagnetic)

(iv) N2→σ1s2, σ*1s2, σ2s2, σ*2s2, σ2pz2, π2px2π2py2 (diamagnetic)

Note here that, if any of the molecular orbital has two electrons, then the electrons will be paired and if it has one electron, then the electron will be unpaired.
